::: {.why}
A more flexible model always fits better in sample, and the point of the last three weeks of machinery is to have the discipline to find out whether it forecasts better.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the dynamic and static hedge ratio versions on the same out-of-sample period with the same costs.
- Say what part of any improvement is explained by the higher turnover the dynamic version induces.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Run both versions over the untouched out-of-sample period with identical cost assumptions, and report Sharpe, turnover and net Sharpe for each. Then hold turnover fixed by damping the dynamic hedge ratio's updates and rerun, so that the comparison is not confounded by trading more.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Write the verdict into reports/milestone-03-pairs.md with the numbers, including the case where the added flexibility does not pay. Note the trial count this comparison added to research_log.jsonl.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The dynamic and static hedge ratio versions of the pairs strategy are compared out of sample at matched turnover, so any improvement is attributable to the estimator rather than to trading more.
:::
